description: 0 = unlimited, overriding config:recommended's prHourlyLimit 2 / prConcurrentLimit 10. Every available update opens a PR immediately rather than queueing in the dashboard's Rate-Limited section. Opening a PR is not deploying -- ArgoCD only acts on what lands on main -- so the cost is PR noise and CI minutes, not risk.

customManagers.description: Bump pinned upstream YAML release URLs (e.g. Gateway API CRDs)

packageRules.description: apps/archive/** is not deployed. The AppSet generators only scan apps/system/*/* and apps/homelab/* (see appsets/), so nothing under archive/ ever reaches the cluster. Renovate was opening PRs for ~6 dead apps.
Homelab container images: grouped. Blast radius is one stateless app each, so an all-or-nothing PR is fine and keeps the queue short.
Homelab Helm charts: grouped, same reasoning.

System charts + the root ArgoCD chart get ONE PR PER DEPENDENCY. No groupName is set for these, and that absence is what splits them. These can take the cluster down (cilium = CNI, longhorn = data, argo-cd = the thing doing the deploying), so each needs its own reviewable diff and its own revert. separateMinorPatch is deliberately NOT set: it opened a second PR for the older line of the same chart (cert-manager 1.20.4 alongside 1.21.2, alloy 1.8.2 alongside 1.12.1, and six more), doubling the queue with PRs that would only ever be closed unread.

Observability travels together. Nothing else in the cluster depends on alloy/loki/tempo/pyroscope/kube-prometheus-stack, and a bad one announces itself immediately in the dashboards it owns, so a single revert of the group is an acceptable blast radius. Majors are excluded and stay individual.

Platform likewise: argo-events, argo-workflows, forgejo, harbor. Self-contained services rather than cluster plumbing. NOTE this excludes root/** deliberately -- argo-cd itself is the thing performing the sync and must never ride along in a group. Majors excluded and stay individual.
Let a release sit before offering it, so yanked or immediately-hotfixed releases never reach a PR.
